identity: The Qur'an, Surat al-Baqara, ayat 172-185, in Uthmani rasm without diacritics (tayyibat written طيبت, al-kitab written الكتب, al-qiyama written القيمة, al-dalala written الضللة, al-salat written الصلوة). Content: lawful and unlawful food, those who conceal revelation, the definition of true righteousness (al-birr), the law of qisas, the bequest, and the ordinance of fasting in Ramadan. 324 tokens, ZERO <NL>.
law: SCRIPTURE: THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (0k). This is the third scripture document I have segmented and the most decisive, because the Qur'anic ayah is not an editorial versification at all - it is part of the revealed text, canonically fixed and traditionally marked by its own end-of-verse sign. When punctuation is stripped, the ayah division IS the sentence division that remains. So I recover the ayah boundaries of al-Baqara 172-185 and take nothing else. Note the unit size differs from the Christian scriptures I have seen (Luke ~14 tokens, Exodus 14.0) - here 324/14 = 23.1 - which is simply because Baqara's legal ayat are long. The LAW is the versification, not any token count.
reasoning: Boundaries: v172 ends ta'budun (13); v173 ghafur rahim (38); v174 'adhab alim (67); v175 al-nar (78); v176 shiqaq ba'id (92); v177 al-muttaqun (143); v178 'adhab alim (180); v179 tattaqun (188); v180 al-muttaqin (204); v181 sami' 'alim (217); v182 ghafur rahim (233); v183 tattaqun (247); v184 ta'lamun (279); v185 tashkurun (323). THE ONE REAL DANGER IN THIS DOCUMENT IS AYAH 177 (tokens 93-143, fifty-one tokens - by far the longest unit I have ever proposed). It contains a huge coordinated list: wa-al-mala'ika wa-al-kitab wa-al-nabiyyin ... wa-ata al-mal ... wa-aqama al-salat wa-ata al-zakat wa-al-mufun bi-'ahdihim ... wa-al-sabirin fi al-ba'sa' wa-al-darra'. This is a textbook trigger for I4 (three or more parallel siblings with no connective is a list, cut before each), for B2 (parallel enumerative clauses each get a unit) and for F1 (long w-chained conjuncts each become a unit). I REFUSE ALL THREE, for three converging reasons: (1) 0k - the ayah is the unit and 2:177 is one ayah; (2) 0t - every member is either a bare NP conjunct or a finite verb inside one continuous relative predication about the single subject 'man amana', i.e. one topic described further, not distinct topics enumerated (0j, 1d); (3) batch 4's doc_02c1581a0f82 and batch 7's etymology chain both showed that a long coordinated chain on ONE topic merges. Firing I4 here would cost me a dozen false cuts in a single verse - precisely the failure mode that took Luke to 83.2. Ayah 185 (280-323, forty-four tokens) is the same situation and gets the same refusal: fa-man shahida ... wa-man kana maridan ... yuridu Allah bikum al-yusr ... wa-li-tukmilu al-'idda wa-li-tukabbiru - all inside one ayah. Other sites refused: the many conditional fa-man ... fa- constructions (@26, @158, @174, @205, @218, @250, @267, @292) are the classic Qur'anic legal shart-jawab, entirely sentence-internal, so B1 (clause-initial fa = CUT) must not fire; wa-lakin at @101 inside 2:177 is refused both by 0q and by the verse law; kama at @240 inside 2:183 likewise. Conversely I DO cut at @144 and @234 even though both open with the same formula ya ayyuha alladhina amanu, because each begins a new ayah - the repeated vocative is a genuine verse opener here, not the E1 parallelism I wrongly fired on 'wayl laka ya Kurzin' in Luke. SANITY CHECK: 14 boundaries / 324 tokens = 23.1 tokens per unit; no unit under 8; consistent with legal Qur'anic ayat.
